short_definition: Analyzing source code or compiled binaries for security vulnerabilities without executing the program.
layman_explanation: Proofreading a book manuscript for typos and flaws before sending it to the printing press.

short_definition: Testing a running application from the outside to discover security vulnerabilities in real time.
layman_explanation: Test-driving a built car on a crash course to see how it handles collisions under real conditions.

short_definition: Combining SAST and DAST techniques using internal software instrumentation during execution.
layman_explanation: Attaching diagnostic sensors inside an engine while test-driving it to monitor internal performance.

short_definition: Automated scanning of open-source components and third-party libraries for known vulnerabilities.
layman_explanation: Checking the ingredients list of a pre-made meal to ensure none of the supplied items are recalled or expired.

short_definition: Injecting malicious code into upstream software dependencies to compromise downstream users.
layman_explanation: Poisoning a water spring high up in the mountains so every town downstream receives contaminated water.

short_definition: Exploiting package managers to pull malicious public packages instead of intended private internal ones.
layman_explanation: Tricking a builder into ordering fake parts from a public market instead of their private trusted warehouse.

short_definition: Integrating security practices seamlessly throughout the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC).
layman_explanation: Building safety inspections directly into the assembly line process rather than inspecting cars only after manufacture.

short_definition: Hardening continuous integration and delivery automation systems against unauthorized code tampering.
layman_explanation: Securing the robotic assembly conveyor belt so unauthorized workers cannot sneak flawed parts into products.

short_definition: Inputting large volumes of invalid, unexpected, or random data into an application to trigger crashes.
layman_explanation: Mashing random keys on a keyboard as fast as possible to see if an application freezes or crashes.

short_definition: A structured procedure for identifying, quantifying, and addressing application security risks during design.
layman_explanation: Sitting down with architectural blueprints to brainstorm every possible way a burglar might enter a house.

short_definition: A mnemonic threat categorization model: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info Disclosure, DoS, Elevation of Privilege.
layman_explanation: A six-point checklist used by engineers to make sure they haven't overlooked common attack vectors.

short_definition: A formal, structured inventory listing all third-party components and libraries comprising a software product.
layman_explanation: A detailed ingredient label on a box of food listing every single component and additive inside.

short_definition: Automated tools scanning code repositories for hardcoded passwords, API keys, and access tokens.
layman_explanation: An automated guard inspecting written code to ensure developers haven't accidentally typed their private keys into public documents.

short_definition: Embedding plaintext passwords or API keys directly within application source code.
layman_explanation: Writing your house key code permanently on the front door mat instead of storing it in a safe.

short_definition: Protecting Application Programming Interfaces from misuse, unauthorized access, and data leakage.
layman_explanation: Ensuring the waiter delivering orders between the kitchen and customers doesn't give away secret recipes.

short_definition: A regularly updated awareness document outlining the most critical security risks for web applications.
layman_explanation: The official 'Top 10 Most Dangerous Mistakes' list every web developer should avoid.

short_definition: Moving security testing earlier in the software development lifecycle to fix bugs before deployment.
layman_explanation: Fixing design mistakes on paper during planning rather than rebuilding a house after construction.

short_definition: Verifying that incoming user data conforms strictly to expected formats, lengths, and types.
layman_explanation: A ticket agent rejecting an entry form if you type numbers into a field meant strictly for your name.

short_definition: Converting potentially dangerous characters into safe, non-executable representations before displaying them.
layman_explanation: Translating special commands into plain display text so browsers treat input as simple words instead of executable instructions.

short_definition: A technique separating SQL code from user-supplied parameters to eliminate SQL injection risks.
layman_explanation: Placing user responses in an isolated glass box so the database never misinterprets user text as database commands.

short_definition: Ensuring application components run with only the permissions required to fulfill their specific functions.
layman_explanation: Giving a dishwasher access to the kitchen sink, but not to the restaurant's cash register.

short_definition: An anomaly where a program writes more data to a buffer than it can hold, corrupting adjacent memory.
layman_explanation: Pouring a gallon of water into a 16-ounce cup until the spill damages nearby electrical outlets.

short_definition: Occurs when an arithmetic operation produces a value beyond the maximum size an integer variable can hold.
layman_explanation: An analog car odometer reaching 999,999 miles and flipping back to 000,000.

short_definition: A flaw where system output depends on the sequence or timing of uncontrollable execution events.
layman_explanation: Two people withdrawing $100 from an account with only $100 in balance at the exact same millisecond.

short_definition: Reconstructing serialized data from untrusted sources, allowing remote code execution or tampering.
layman_explanation: Unpacking a compressed wooden furniture flat-pack without checking if someone hid a bomb inside the box.

short_definition: An attacker introducing malicious code into a computer program that is subsequently executed.
layman_explanation: Slipping malicious script lines into an automated teleprompter so the news anchor speaks unapproved words.

short_definition: A unique, unpredictable secret token generated by a server to validate submitted user requests.
layman_explanation: A unique hand-stamp required alongside your password every single time you submit a web form.

short_definition: A set of rules and best practices developers follow to eliminate security flaws during coding.
layman_explanation: Building codes and safety standards that plumbers and electricians must follow when wiring a house.

short_definition: A security technology embedded inside an application that monitors runtime behavior and blocks threats.
layman_explanation: An internal immune system inside an app that detects malicious activity and shuts down dangerous tasks instantly.

short_definition: Systematic examination of software source code intended to find security bugs missed in development.
layman_explanation: Having a second senior editor read through an article line-by-line to check for critical errors before publishing.

short_definition: An authorized simulated attack on a computer system to evaluate its security strength.
layman_explanation: Hiring a friendly professional burglar to try breaking into your building so you can fix weak windows.

short_definition: A reward program offering monetary compensation to independent researchers for reporting security vulnerabilities.
layman_explanation: Offering a cash reward to anyone in the public who finds a flaw in your house security system.

short_definition: Guidelines explaining how ethical hackers can safely submit security flaw reports to an organization.
layman_explanation: Posting a clear sign on your website saying 'If you find a security hole, please email us here safely.'

short_definition: Publishing malicious open-source packages with names similar to popular libraries (e.g., 'reqeusts' vs 'requests').
layman_explanation: Creating a fake tool named 'reqeusts' hoping software developers accidentally download it due to a typing mistake.

short_definition: Gaining unauthorized access to a popular source code repository to insert backdoors into official releases.
layman_explanation: Sneaking into a blueprint factory to alter official building plans before contractors receive them.

short_definition: Directives sent by web servers telling browsers how to handle security mechanisms like CSP and HSTS.
layman_explanation: Instruction sheets attached to outgoing packages telling handlers exactly how securely to store them.

short_definition: Limiting the number of API requests a user or client can make within a designated timeframe.
layman_explanation: Allowing customers to order only 3 drinks per hour to prevent disruptive behavior.

short_definition: Restricting network request rates to prevent server overload and brute-force password guessing.
layman_explanation: Allowing only 5 incorrect password attempts per minute before locking the login box.

short_definition: Appointing developers within teams to act as security advocates and peer advisors.
layman_explanation: Designating one team member in every department as the designated safety warden.

short_definition: Minimizing the total number of exposed vulnerabilities that an attacker could exploit.
layman_explanation: Boarding up unused windows and doors on a building so burglars have fewer entry points.

short_definition: Automatically terminating active sessions after periods of user inactivity to prevent unauthorized access.
layman_explanation: Automatically logging off your banking app if you leave your screen untouched for 5 minutes.

short_definition: Stripping dangerous HTML and JavaScript tags from user inputs before saving or rendering them.
layman_explanation: A strainer removing big stones and debris from water before pouring it into a pitcher.

short_definition: Adding special escape characters to user input so databases treat special symbols as literal text.
layman_explanation: Putting quotation marks around user words so the computer knows they are just plain text, not code instructions.

short_definition: Explicitly declaring which form fields an application is permitted to update in the database.
layman_explanation: Giving a guest a checklist of 3 items they are allowed to edit on their profile, ignoring all other form inputs.

short_definition: Replacing direct database IDs in URLs with temporary session-specific random tokens to prevent IDOR.
layman_explanation: Giving customers temporary cloakroom ticket numbers instead of revealing their actual file cabinet drawer number.

short_definition: Removing unnecessary features, services, and default configurations to secure an application.
layman_explanation: Stripping away unnecessary doors, extra keys, and decorative windows from a high-security vault.

short_definition: An engineering approach where security is foundational to system architecture rather than added later.
layman_explanation: Designing a car with built-in seatbelts and airbags from scratch instead of taping safety gear on afterward.

short_definition: Configuring software so that its default settings provide the highest level of security out of the box.
layman_explanation: A new smartphone arriving with its lock screen, encryption, and firewall turned on automatically.

short_definition: Designing application error handling to default to a secure closed state when failures occur.
layman_explanation: An electronic vault door automatically locking shut when power cuts out, rather than popping open.

short_definition: Locking software package dependencies to exact tested version numbers to prevent untested auto-updates.
layman_explanation: Ordering the exact 2024 model of a car part every time instead of accepting random new versions automatically.

short_definition: Ensuring that compiling the same source code repeatedly yields identical binary output files.
layman_explanation: Baking a cake using a strict recipe that guarantees every bakery produces the exact same result down to the gram.

short_definition: Creating pre-configured, security-tested master virtual machine or container templates.
layman_explanation: Using a single pre-approved, perfectly secure master keycard design for every employee badge.

short_definition: Measuring the time taken to execute cryptographic functions to deduce secret key details.
layman_explanation: Guessing a password by measuring how many extra milliseconds the computer takes to compare each letter.

short_definition: Designing software microservices to authenticate and verify every internal inter-service API call.
layman_explanation: Requiring employees to show their badge every time they move between rooms inside the same office.
